steps.title: Sex is a stain, not a second brain
steps.narration: Most of this CNS is isomorphic — same types as the female. Gold is male-specific. Rust is sexually dimorphic: the type exists in both sexes, wired differently here. Everything else stays mute.

steps.title: Male-specific cells
steps.narration: About 1,250 neurons with no female counterpart in this annotation. Most sit in the central brain. This is the circuit the male CNS was built to see.

steps.title: Shared but different
steps.narration: Sexually dimorphic types exist in both sexes. Here their numbers, shape, or partners changed. The paper's 114 dimorphic types live in this gold-rust scatter.

steps.title: fruitless
steps.narration: High fruitless expression marks many courtship cells. It is a genetic handle, not a synonym for male-specific — some fru cells are isomorphic.

steps.title: doublesex
steps.narration: doublesex and fru/dsx coexpression. Fewer cells than fruitless, often closer to the sexual dimorphism labels.

steps.title: Dimorphic commands
steps.narration: A handful of descending neurons are themselves male-specific or dimorphic: pIP10, aSP22, DNp13, and DNg02. They are how a male-specific brain talks to a body.
